Memento comparison I ran: 20260910185345 has Crunchbase=0, Quartr=6; 20260911101011 has Crunchbase=19, Quartr=0 (Crunchbase added and the error-rate chart removed); 20260911215402 additionally has Fiscal.ai=9. unsupported.fact: #27 — 'this is a live document: the 2026-09-10 launch version and the 2026-09-14 version differ in at least three places; the article must state it relies on the 2026-09-14 version'
unsupported.why: Mis-dated and undercounted. The edits happened on 2026-09-11, in two steps, and the page has been stable from 2026-09-11 21:54 UTC through the newest capture at 2026-09-14 01:29 UTC. There are at least seven distinct changes, not three: intro provider list gains Crunchbase; 'Premium financial data' provider list gains Crunchbase; Crunchbase testimonial + Jager McConnell added; Fiscal.ai testimonial + Braden Dennis added; 'like S&P Global and FactSet' removed from the MCP paragraph; FactSet added to the connector-ecosystem list; the 'Error rate' chart (Quartr 5.09%->1.99%, S&P Global 6.84%->2.66%, FactSet 9.59%->6.45%, Daloopa 7.53%->2.57%) and its caption removed. The correct wording for the article is 'the version live since 2026-09-11', not 'the 2026-09-14 version'.

unsupported.fact: #28 — 'the official ChatGPT product documentation pricing page lists the plans as Free $0/mo, Go $8/mo, Plus $20/mo, Pro from $100/mo, Business $20/user/mo (2+ users, billed annually, $25 monthly), Enterprise & Edu contact sales'
unsupported.why: Every figure is correct as printed and 'zero mentions of Financial Services' is correct (0 hits for 'financial'), but the framing is wrong. The page frames all of these as CODEX plans: the switcher id is codex-pricing-plans and the subtitles read 'Explore Codex capabilities on quick coding tasks', 'Use Codex for lightweight coding tasks', 'Power a few focused coding sessions each week', 'Bring Codex into your startup or growing business', 'Unlock Codex for your entire organization'. A seventh card, 'API Key' (no price, 'Pay for Codex usage based on API pricing'), is omitted entirely. Recorded as a flat list of ChatGPT plan prices this invites the writer to drop $8/$20/$100 into an article about an enterprise product that has no published price. Narrow the fact to what it supports: OpenAI's own ChatGPT product documentation publishes no price for ChatGPT for Financial Services.

additional_findings: SOURCING CHALLENGE — the researcher's 'full' verdict does not hold. Two structural problems. (1) The entire substance of the article comes from a page that returns 403 here; every body fact was read from web.archive.org. The Internet Archive is a verbatim capture of the first-party page and is not an aggregator, but BRIEF.md's rule for a 403 is '換同一官方站的其他頁、官方 RSS… 查到的事實如果只存在於被擋的頁面後面，那就不寫'. This route is not authorised by the spec, and the pack would ship a sources[0] url nobody on the team can open. (2) The other three sources (learn.chatgpt.com pricing / ChatGPT Work overview / Plugin controls) contain ZERO mentions of ChatGPT for Financial Services — I confirmed 0 hits for 'financial' in pricing.md and in llms.txt (323 lines). They support background and negatives only. The pack therefore has one substantive source, against BRIEF's 至少 2 條一手來源. The editor must either accept the archive route explicitly (and have the article say so in its own body) or treat B8 as blocked.
MISSING — the article's own one-line positioning, the hero subhead 'Frontier intelligence, built for financial services.' Not recorded anywhere in the research record.

MISSING — the plain-language capability paragraph, the single most usable sentence for a lay Taiwanese reader, absent from all 34 facts: 'It can navigate and understand figures, tables, and the supporting notes in financial documents. It can take inputs, run financial analysis, and draw conclusions. And it can take all of this work and accurately synthesize it into documents, spreadsheets, and slides.'

MISSING — the only place the page says current coverage is not final: 'Our partners are central to this work and as we expand coverage, we will continue to deepen our models' understanding of these datasets. We will post train our models to find, interpret, and use this data like we know the best analysts can.'

MISSING — the interactive-charts feature entirely: 'We've built fundamental capabilities into the product so that it can research across multiple sources, trace figures across different periods, and interpret annotations in public data. Once that analysis is complete, teams can build interactive charts and visualizations.' plus the caption 'Compare company performance in interactive charts, with the underlying data and sources available for review.'

MISSING — the whole 'Expanding what the industry can achieve' section, where OpenAI itself hedges that one product will not cover the industry ('we recognize that it will require a range of solutions') and says firms and developers can use the API to build their own applications. Material framing.

MISSING — the section-opening paragraph 'ChatGPT for Financial Services brings together the financial data teams need, with the depth of detail expected. We've included premium financial data, streamlined existing provider connections, and improved MCP performance.', OpenAI's own three-part summary of the data story.

MISSING — the current 9/14 MCP sentence is never recorded as a fact, only as a diff: 'It can be challenging to effectively use MCP connectors for data providers. We have focused on making some of the most used MCPs in financial services optimized for immediate use in the product, so teams can spend less time troubleshooting requests and more time on analysis.' Also missing captions 'ChatGPT for Financial Services brings together built-in data, connected sources, and financial analysis workflows.' and 'Publish firm templates to the teams who use them.', and the prefooter block 'Bring ChatGPT for Financial Services to your firm' / 'Equip your teams with GPT-6 Astra, included financial data, and new tools for research, financial modeling, and client materials.'

SPEC COMPLIANCE — hero_label 'AI 進投行，先看得懂來源' is 13 characters against BRIEF's 繁中 ≤ 12 字 limit; title is still the placeholder '（撰稿時填入 zh-TW title，≤ 60 字）' and diagram.caption is a placeholder, both required by the research-record schema; diagram node '四家資料商直接可用' asserts a hard count of four, but the page says 'providers like …' (non-exhaustive) and separately presents Fiscal.ai as a data partner with a CEO quote and a logo tab — the researcher's own excluded #4 and must_not_write #9 already flag that tension, so the diagram contradicts them.

The researcher reported the CDX API as 'Temporarily Offline' and fell back to timestamp redirects; the timemap gives the full list and is how I pinned the edits to 2026-09-11.

SURVIVED THE ATTACK — the three benchmark facts are exactly right. OfficeQA Pro chart values GPT-6 Astra 69.9 / GPT-5.6 Sol 60.2 / Claude Fable 5.1 62.4 (y-axis 'Correctness'); BoxBench 0.77 / 0.74 / 0.72 (y-axis 'Weighted rubric accuracy'); slide chart title ["Slides Head to Head (Internal)","Versus Opus 5"], y-axis 'Win Rate (Human Eval)', values GPT-5.5 0.216 / GPT-5.6 Sol 0.306 / GPT-6 Astra 0.556 while the caption says 'only 21.6% for GPT-5.6 Sol'. The caption/data contradiction is real and present in BOTH versions, and the decision to publish only 55.6% is correct. All three captions are verbatim as recorded, and all three are correctly marked is_vendor_claim.

SURVIVED THE ATTACK — facts #2, #4–#23, #25, #26, #29–#33 are all verbatim-correct against pages I fetched myself. The six named executives in #26 all check out (Jager McConnell CEO Crunchbase; Thomas Li CEO Daloopa; Tom Van Buskirk EVP of Technology and Engineering PitchBook; Braden Dennis CEO Fiscal.ai; Sally Moore Chief Client Officer and Co-Head of Market Intelligence, Kensho Data & Platforms at S&P Global; Emily Prince Group Head of Enterprise AI, LSEG).
